title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI agent was used to conduct post-exploitation attacks after an initial vulnerability in marimo was exploited. The agent moved from initial access through extracting cloud credentials, retrieving SSH keys, and exfiltrating a PostgreSQL database in under one hour. The agent made decisions in real time rather than executing a predetermined script, adapting its actions based on information gathered at each stage.

The system was deployed in an environment where it had access to cloud credentials and database keys without human oversight of its actions. Detection occurred through analysis of command signatures that showed planning behavior, improvisation against unknown targets, and use of previous output to inform subsequent commands. A human operator monitoring the AI agent's access or reviewing its proposed actions before execution could have interrupted the attack chain.

Whether the AI agent was deliberately designed for this attack or repurposed from another use case is not established.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
# Summary

On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team detected an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent executed a cyberattack in real time rather than following a pre-written script. The attacker exploited a vulnerability called CVE-2026-39987 in a marimo notebook application to gain initial access, then extracted cloud credentials and used them to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager. The attacker subsequently used this key to access an internal server and dump an entire PostgreSQL database containing sensitive information like API keys and user credentials. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to database theft, completed in under one hour, with the database exfiltration happening in just two minutes.

The research team identified four distinct signatures proving the attack was driven by an AI agent rather than automated scripts or human operators. These signatures included improvised commands against unknown targets, planning comments in the command stream, machine-readable command formatting, and intelligent use of previous output to inform subsequent actions. The Sysdig team recommends immediately updating marimo to version 0.23.0 or later, auditing exposed systems for compromised credentials, rotating all AWS credentials and database passwords, and deploying runtime threat detection across networks.
